study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Fraza et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Unraveling the link between CNVs, cognition and individual neuroimaging deviation scores from a population-based reference cohort

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states aims and hypotheses and explains why normative modeling is used. It aims to map individualized brain deviation scores for pathogenic CNV carriers using normative models, and explicitly hypothesizes that CNV carriers will show larger deviation scores and high inter-individual variability. This directly satisfies both criteria (stated research questions/hypotheses and purpose of applying normative modeling).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here we aim to map individualized brain deviation scores in individuals with pathogenic CNVs. We used normative modeling to map neuroimaging features from several large neuroimaging datasets and applied these models to understand the neurobiological profile of CNV carriers in the UK Biobank cohort." … "We hypothesize that (1) individuals with a CNV related to cognitive deficits or neurodevelopmental disorders will have larger deviation scores compared with a reference model across several brain areas and (2) that the patterns of deviation across brain regions will be highly variable between these CNV carriers."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: A new voxel-wise normative model is built from pooled public datasets. The data sources and overall QC approach are described, including visual inspection and final sample size after QC. However, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria and reasons for exclusion are not comprehensively specified beyond visual QC, and explicit image quality thresholds are not provided. Thus, some but not all criteria are met.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "To create the voxel-wise Jacobian normative model that spans the entire age range, we pooled a large dataset from five publicly available repositories: Cam-CAN, HCP, Oasis, PNC and UK Biobank…" … "In total, we used visually quality-controlled T1 Jacobian data from 19,620 participants from seven sites." … "Visual inspection was performed to ensure data quality… resulting in a total of 19,620 participants with MRI scans passing the quality control assessment."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Fraza2023.pdf.md — Methods: Participant demographics and data sources; Fraza2023_sup1.pdf.md — Data - Whole brain voxel-wise Jacobian model

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The model includes age and sex, and adds site as a fixed effect to address multi-site variation, explicitly describing the approach to site effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Every normative model constructed factored in the covariates age and sex. To reduce site effects, we have added it as a fixed effect in the model." … "The resulting models accounted for as much as 52% of the variation… using the covariates age, sex and site."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Fraza2023.pdf.md — Methods: Normative modeling with Bayesian linear regression; Results text near Fig. 3

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing steps and software are described for the voxel-wise model (FSL FLIRT/FNIRT; generation of Jacobian determinant images). Quality control via visual inspection is also mentioned. For IDPs, preprocessing via FUNPACK is cited.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The data were preprocessed with a registration to a standard spatial reference using FSL's FLIRT and FNIRT, with the commands cmd_fsl_anat and cmd_add_affine… Within the framework of a voxel-based model, we opted for the Jacobian determinants (T1_to_MNI_aff+nonlin_jac.nii.gz)." … "IDPs … were processed using FUNPACK (v.2.8)… for automatic normalization, cleaning and parsing."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is detailed: Bayesian linear regression with B-spline basis and likelihood warping (Sinarcsinh), Gaussian prior, Powell optimization, implemented using PCNtoolkit; covariates specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "We employed the Bayesian linear regression function from the PCNtoolkit… The analysis used a Gaussian prior… To ensure accurate modeling of nonlinear and non-Gaussian effects, we employed a B-spline basis function and likelihood warping…" … "Python version 3.8 and PCNtoolkit version 0.28 were used… Sinarcsinh likelihood warping and Powell optimization."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Secondary data from UK Biobank are used. The original CNV calling publication is cited and key QC thresholds for CNV calls are summarized. Final sample sizes of CNV carriers are reported. However, detailed imaging quality standards specific to the clinical subset and explicit reasons for exclusions are limited.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "We identified CNVs based on the returned dataset from Crawford et al. For details on the preprocessing and calling pipeline and quality control of the CNVs see… Briefly, their quality control included genotypic call rate <0.96, waviness factor of <-0.03 and >0.03, >30 CNVs per person, and log R ratio s.d. of >0.35." … "Among the participants with quality-controlled Jacobian neuroimaging data, 375 individuals had a pathogenic CNV."
